questions.question: Explain what is meant by corporate social responsibility and give two examples of how a business might demonstrate it.

points.text: CSR means a business takes responsibility for its effects on stakeholders and society beyond legal requirements. Examples: sourcing sustainable materials, paying the living wage, supporting local charities, reducing packaging waste.

questions.question: Analyse how pressure groups can influence a business's decisions.

points.text: Pressure groups use tactics such as: organising boycotts (reducing sales), media campaigns (damaging reputation), lobbying government (leading to stricter regulation), and protests outside premises. Businesses may respond by changing practices to avoid negative publicity and maintain customer loyalty.

questions.question: Evaluate whether a clothing retailer should switch to using only fair trade cotton, even though it will increase costs by 15%.

points.text: Arguments for: ethical reputation attracts conscious consumers (growing market), improves brand loyalty, motivates employees who value ethics, reduces risk of scandals, meets CSR commitments. Arguments against: 15% cost increase may reduce profit margins, prices may rise making products less competitive, fair trade certification has administrative costs, not all customers will pay more. questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate whether a coffee shop chain should commit to using only Fairtrade coffee beans. <div class="

points.text: A grade 9 response will: consider cost implications (Fairtrade premium of ~10%), customer response (some willing to pay more, others price-sensitive), competitive position (differentiation vs cost disadvantage), supplier relationships (more stable, better quality), employee motivation (proud to work for ethical brand). Conclude: the Fairtrade premium is a worthwhile investment for a chain targeting socially conscious consumers, as the brand differentiation and loyalty offset higher costs. For a budget chain competing on price, the cost increase may be harder to absorb.
